metadata.title: Sugar #11 — El Niño + Hormuz Compound Thesis
metadata.subtitle: Feb'27 SBG7 18¢ calls × 2 · executed May 22, 2026

thesis.headline: Thesis confirming: El Niño Advisory ACTIVE (NOAA, Aug 2026) + all three forecasters revised deeper into deficit in August. Entered 15.0¢ — sugar now ~16.7¢, highest since March.
thesis.summary: Every leg is moving the right way: India's monsoon is tracking 12% below normal (IMD warns Aug–Sep below normal; possibly weakest in 11 years), Brazil's Center-South mills have pivoted hard to ethanol (sugar mix 41.4% vs 50.1% last year, output -2.0% YoY), and El Niño is forecast to peak very strong Oct–Jan. Deficit revisions are accelerating, not stabilizing.

elNino.probabilityWindow: El Niño Advisory ACTIVE (NOAA CPC, Aug 2026) — event formed and intensifying
elNino.soiNote: Atmospheric coupling confirmed — all 30 GFDL ensemble members peak among strongest events on record (Aug 2026 update)

millMix.brazilOutputNote: 2026/27 through May: sugar mix collapsed to 41.4% (from 50.1% a year ago) as mills pivot to ethanol — C-S sugar output 6.84 MMT, -2.0% YoY. This is the 'mill mix shift' leg of the tail scenario actually happening.

catalystTimeline.event: Indian monsoon — LIVE: 12% below normal cumulative (Aug 10); IMD warns Aug–Sep below normal, possibly weakest in 11 years
El Niño peak intensity — NOAA: very strong peak likely Oct–Jan (63% ≥ +2.0°C)

managementRules: Profit-take 1: Sell 50% at 200% return on premium
Stop trigger: IV crashes below 18% on ceasefire news
Time stop: Reassess at 60 DTE if not ITM

exitTriggers.name: El Niño weakens / fails
exitTriggers.rationale: Was the primary risk — now largely retired: NOAA Advisory active, 97% persistence through early spring 2027, 23/26 models very strong. Residual risk is a weaker-than-forecast peak.

exitTriggers.name: Hormuz ceasefire IV crush
exitTriggers.rationale: Options re-price down even before underlying moves. Pre-expiry risk.

exitTriggers.name: Brazilian mill mix stays at sugar
exitTriggers.rationale: Mills keep flooding market above ethanol parity.

exitTriggers.name: India ethanol policy reversal
exitTriggers.rationale: Govt raises diversion → removes export supply (bullish risk for sugar but kills bear setup).

exitTriggers.name: Theta decay without move
exitTriggers.rationale: ~$3-5/day per OTM call. Manageable but compounds if no move by Q4.

tailScenario.title: Energy Lockdown → Sugar Deficit

components.mechanism: Brazilian mill mix shift to ethanol

tailScenario.context: 2024/25 deficit was 3.5 MMT → drove sugar +100% to 28¢. Lockdown deficit could be 2-3x larger.
tailScenario.inelasticDemandNote: Sugar is staple food. COVID: consumption fell 3-5%, recovered fast. 1973-74 energy crisis: consumption fell <10%, prices rose 6x.

personalView.executionTarget: EXECUTED May 22: 2 × Feb'27 SBG7 18¢ calls @ 0.88¢ avg ($1,977 cost basis)
executionNotes: Verify actual Mar'27 ATM strike — sugar may have moved
Check bid-ask: if >5 ticks wide on 19¢, move to more liquid strike (18¢ or 20¢)
Check IV: fair = 22-28%, if 35%+ news has moved without us
personalView.sizingLogic: Sugar at 20-30% of oil book notional (satellite, not core). Don't size up at entry — add into confirming trend (India monsoon data, Brazilian mix reports).

executedPosition.notes: Selected 18¢ strike vs planned 19¢ — slightly closer to ATM, marginally less asymmetric but higher delta (0.364 vs ~0.30 estimate for 19¢). Feb'27 expiry vs planned Mar'27 — one less month of time value but catches all major catalysts (Indian monsoon Jun-Sep, Brazilian C-S Aug-Oct, El Niño peak Nov-Feb). Net: cleaner risk-reward with marginally tighter convexity.
